explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/80 (Erdős–Rothschild): f_c(n) is the maximal m such that every n-vertex graph with at least cn² edges, each edge in a triangle, contains a book of size m; the problem asks to estimate f_c(n), whether f_c(n) > n^ε, or whether f_c(n) ≫ log n. In the formalization, bookNumber G is the maximum over edges of the number of triangles (3-cliques) containing the edge, and f c n is the sInf of bookNumber over admissible graphs on Fin n, which is exactly the largest forced book size. The statement ∀ c ∈ (0, 1/2), (f c n) ≫ log n unfolds via the project notation to log n = O(f c n) at atTop, i.e. f_c(n) ≫_c log n for each fixed c, matching the source. The restriction c < 1/2 is necessary and harmless: for c ≥ 1/2 no graph has cn² edges and sInf ∅ = 0 makes the claim false for trivial reasons, while for c < 1/2 K_n is admissible for all large n so the junk value only affects finitely many n. For c > 1/4 the claim follows from f_c(n) ≥ n/6, so the content is c ≤ 1/4, where Fox–Loh give n^{O(1/log log n)} upper bounds and only regularity-type lower bounds are known; the page lists no resolution of the log n question, so 'research open' and the yes/no `question` tag are appropriate.
